condition: Rapidly enlarging thyroid mass with stridor (anaplastic carcinoma / lymphoma)
summary: 76-year-old woman with Hashimoto's thyroiditis and a hard neck mass that has doubled in 3 weeks, now with stridor, hoarseness and dysphagia. Anaplastic carcinoma or thyroid lymphoma: airway first (senior anaesthesia/ENT), urgent core biopsy (FNA may miss lymphoma), rapid staging; not an elective thyroidectomy pathway.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Neck swelling growing fast and noisy breathing
inputs.hpi: Known Hashimoto's thyroiditis on levothyroxine. Neck swelling on the left has doubled in size over 3 weeks. Voice hoarse for 2 weeks, food sticking, and noisy breathing at night for 3 days, now also when walking. Lost 5 kg.

exam.general: Audible inspiratory stridor at rest, speaking in sentences, RR 26, SpO2 93% on air. 7 cm hard, fixed, irregular left thyroid mass extending across the midline, trachea deviated to the right. Hard left cervical nodes. Unable to get below the mass.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Rapidly enlarging thyroid mass with stridor — suspected anaplastic thyroid carcinoma vs primary thyroid lymphoma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Rapidly enlarging hard thyroid mass with stridor at rest, hoarseness and dysphagia on a background of Hashimoto's — anaplastic carcinoma vs lymphoma. Airway: senior anaesthetic and ENT review now, humidified oxygen, dexamethasone. Urgent core biopsy, CT neck/chest, haematology/oncology MDT.

mustNotMiss.note: Rapid growth over weeks with stridor in an older patient (Hashimoto's): anaplastic carcinoma and thyroid lymphoma are the diagnoses to name.

mustAlarm.note: Any emergency alarm counts here (the generic triage alarm included).
An alarm that names the airway problem, so the response is airway-directed.

mustInclude.note: ATA 2021: core or open biopsy when FNA cannot distinguish anaplastic carcinoma from lymphoma.

mustExclude.note: A templated elective total-thyroidectomy plan is not the next step for a stridulous, probably unresectable anaplastic/lymphoma mass.

guideline.name: 2021 ATA guidelines — anaplastic thyroid cancer
guideline.section: Rapid diagnosis (core or open biopsy when FNA is non-diagnostic; exclude lymphoma), airway assessment and management, rapid staging, BRAF testing, multidisciplinary decision on resection
guideline.citation: Bible KC, Kebebew E, Brierley J, et al. 2021 American Thyroid Association guidelines for management of patients with anaplastic thyroid cancer. Thyroid. 2021;31:337–386.

guideline.name: British Thyroid Association guidelines — management of thyroid cancer
guideline.section: Investigation of thyroid nodules (TFTs, ultrasound, FNAC); urgent referral features (stridor, rapidly enlarging mass, voice change); anaplastic carcinoma and lymphoma
guideline.citation: Perros P, Boelaert K, Colley S, et al. Guidelines for the management of thyroid cancer. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf). 2014;81(Suppl 1):1–122.

rationale: Must-not-miss thyroid emergency. Tests the airway alarm, emergency level, naming of anaplastic carcinoma/lymphoma, and biopsy strategy (core rather than FNA).
